Representative_Docs: ['Can I run a job when the pipeline is an MR _and_ no changes are being made to a specified path?. In GitLab CI, I can specify that a job should run if the pipeline is for a merge request. I can also run a job if changes are being made to a certain file (or set of files). This I would do with the following rules: Check Changelog Existence: script: - echo "Changelog files exist" rules: - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event" changes: - changelogs/unreleased/**/* This is fine and dandy... but what I actually want to do is almost the exact opposite. That is, I want a job to fail if a merge request does NOT have changelog entry files. Is there some way for me to do that, preferably using the GitLab CI DSL? I know I can perform some hoop jumping and do this in the script but that is a bit messy and I\'d prefer to do it using only the GitLab CI YAML if possible. The following GitLab CI YAML does work for me, but as I said, I would like to know if this can be achieved without resorting to manually run the git CLI in a script. Check Changelog Existence: image: alpine/git variables: GIT_DEPTH: "0" # Tells git to fetch all the branches of the project, required by the analysis task script: - git --no-pager diff --name-status remotes/origin/$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME | grep ^A | grep changelogs/unreleased/ # Ensure that some files have been added to the unreleased changelog path rules: - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event" when: always', 'GitLab CI: How to use variables defined in workflow in `rules` of other jobs?. I\'m trying to use a variable defined in workflow in the rules section of a job. Here is a pipeline with two very similar jobs: variables: GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK_NAME_PRODUCTION: "production" workflow: rules: - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main" variables: GOOGLE_PLAY_DEPLOYMENT_TRACK: $GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK_NAME_PRODUCTION stages: - setup this-runs: stage: setup image: python:3.13.3 script: - echo $GOOGLE_PLAY_DEPLOYMENT_TRACK - echo $GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK_NAME_PRODUCTION rules: - if: $GOOGLE_PLAY_DEPLOYMENT_TRACK this-should-run: stage: setup image: python:3.13.3 script: - echo $GOOGLE_PLAY_DEPLOYMENT_TRACK - echo $GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK_NAME_PRODUCTION rules: - if: $GOOGLE_PLAY_DEPLOYMENT_TRACK == $GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK_NAME_PRODUCTION When deploying to main , I expect both of those to run. However, the second of those is not even scheduled for execution. This can be verified by pasting the above snippet in GitLab Pipeline Editor and going to validate (requiring main to be the default branch). How can I compare the value of a workflow defined variable to the value of a script-variable and use the result to determine which jobs to execute?', 'How to set up parent pipeline for different triggers commit messages and web button?. Name: 11_image_cache_gitlab_downloading
Representative_Docs: ['How to cache pnpm in Gitlab CI. So I\'m trying to use pnpm inside of a pipeline, with efficient caching . There were similar questions already ( Use pnpm in diferent Gitlab CI stages ) but they do not address all the aspects of caching and some of the answers do not work for me. I also found some information on the internet that seem contrary to everything else I\'ve read, so I would like to clarify it. For example: Some people say that cache is not meant for passing data from job to job in the same pipeline, and it should be an artifact instead. In their view cache is only meant for sharing files between different pipelines: https://dev-tips.com/gitlab/difference-between-caches-and-artifacts-in-gitlab-ci Some people use separate "install" job for example in .pre stage for installing dependencies. But does it make sense to have this "empty" job?
